Sean/Laura — quick triage notes (raw):
- Confirmed: a 6-minute reservation gap occurred in the US-dedicated pool that hosts Horizon's reserved capacity. The autoscaler briefly rebalanced capacity after a noisy neighbor (long unquantized model variant) triggered higher GPU memory pressure.
- Impact: token-level throttling for priority-route requests; p99 latency increased from ~850ms to ~3.2s; 5xx rate rose because upstream queuing overflowed into early termination.
- Cause hypothesis: kernel fallback on a single host due to an unoptimized attention pattern for the reconciliation model variant + insufficient prefix cache hit rate.

Mitigation actions performed (00:40–00:58 UTC):
1) Manually pinned Horizon's routes to the remaining dedicated heads to prevent spill-to-general pool.
2) Applied an emergency soft-quantization profile to the hot model path to reduce per-token compute (risk: minor quality delta).
3) Enabled cross-region spillover to the EU-warmed spare cluster (temporary) — latency tradeoff but preserves throughput.

Attached: svc-ops-runbook.pdf (runbook excerpt), capacity-heatmap-1127.png (capacity timeline).

Next steps:
- We need leadership approval to keep cross-region spillover on for the next 36 hours while we finish a kernel-level patch and a longer-term scheduling fix.
- I recommend we issue a one-time credit if SLA windows are missed; Finance+Sales will need to confirm.

David Kim
